Explanation: Appears to work because different regNos produce distinct objects, and reference equality (==) suppresses re-adding bs1.

Without hashCode(), Object.hashCode uses memory address; objects land in different buckets so equals() is never called. With overridden hashCode(), both map to same bucket and duplicate is eliminated.
Object remains in HashSet (size=1) but contains() returns FALSE! The new hashCode places lookup in a different bucket. Demonstrates why hash fields must be final/immutable.
